about: T1.33 part 2's acceptance tests that failed when the independent test author wrote them, before the implementation, on origin/rust-core-phase-1 at f5826d81: contract/tests/test_t133_type_set.py and rust/crates/sdm-host/tests/t133_type_set.rs over contract/type-set-vectors.json (every arrow-rs DataType classified, with its received-type inference vector; a difference from the reference registered; HOST-2's types marked), and contract/tests/test_t133_register.py (no proposed entry without its approver, named in its notes as 'Approver: owner' or 'Approver: reviewer'; every changed case named; P1B-1 replaced case by case; the owner's answers of 2026-10-13 night recorded: P1B-36, P1B-5, P1B-6, DT-14 and ORD-1 approved, P1B-1 to P1B-4 closed as superseded, C9 and H11 confirmed, DT-7 the reviewer's). 'rust-host' holds type-set vector ids (none failed: the core admits and infers every type as its vector says, by name), 'exits' the Python test ids, 'py:<test id>'. Each listed test must still fail (strict); the implementer takes an id out of 'pending' once it passes, and changes nothing else: 'pending' stays within 'authored', which is the test author's. Added after Codex's review of part 2 (on 0bb1970d): five vectors marked 'not reachable' are reachable through DuckDB 1.5.6, each now with its 'witness' statements; four differ from the reference (dictionary.uint16-utf8 and dictionary.uint32-utf8, ENUMs of 300 and 70000 members; struct.large-utf8 and map.large-utf8-int64 under arrow_large_buffer_size), their registration tests pending until approved entries name them; timestamp.us.utc succeeds on both.
